title: Beyond the 956: Derrick Harriott, Jamaican ska, rocksteady and reggae pioneer, dies at 87
excerpt: Derrick Harriott, the Jamaican singer and producer behind 'The Loser' who helped shape ska, rocksteady and reggae, has died at 87 at his home in St. Andrew, Jamaica.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Derrick Harriott, the Jamaican singer and producer who helped carry his country's music from ska through rocksteady and into reggae — and whose signature hit "The Loser" became a classic of the era — has died at 87.

Harriott died at his home in St. Andrew, Jamaica, shortly after 1:00 a.m. on Saturday, October 24, 2026, after a period of illness, according to Dorrel Mattocks, operator of the Derrick Harriott Music Store, who confirmed the death to The Gleaner. Harriott had recently been discharged from hospital before returning home. No specific cause of death has been officially reported.

Born February 6, 1939, in Kingston, Harriott began his musical career in the late 1950s. In 1958 he co-founded the vocal group The Jiving Juniors, recording early hits including "Lollipop Girl" and "Over the River." He went solo in 1962 and launched his own Crystal record label, releasing "I Care" and his signature song "The Loser," along with "Solomon," "Walk the Streets" and "What Can I Do."

As a producer, Harriott helped shape early reggae and dub, working with Dennis Brown, Big Youth, The Ethiopians, Keith & Tex and The Kingstonians. His studio band, the Crystallites, recorded the instrumental album Undertaker, and Scrub A Dub (1974), mixed at King Tubby's studio, was one of the earliest dub albums. Swing magazine named him top producer of 1970.

His contribution to Jamaican music earned him the Order of Distinction in 2009 and the Jamaica Reggae Industry Association Lifetime Achievement Award in 2019. He also ran a beloved Kingston record shop, first on King Street and later at Twin Gates Plaza in Half-Way Tree.

Sources: Caribbean Media Corporation (CMC) wire report; The Jamaica Gleaner, via Dorrel Mattocks; The Jamaica Observer, via Clash Music.
